blockingIssues.description: Browser-originated sign-in started from `/auth?redirect=...` never auto-returns to the requested trusted destination because the web auth entrypoint only auto-navigates when device-flow handoff state exists.
The milestone contract requires admins to revoke/cancel pending org invites cleanly, but the landed broker and web evidence never proves a successful pending org-invite revoke path.

Repo-bound CLI ownership output ignores broker registrations unless local config already says `ownership.mode === "shared"`, so a default-local repo can disagree with the new web project registration state and hide shared/local conflicts.

nonBlockingIssues.description: Management-token `/v1/auth/me` hydration can still leave verified users with `emailVerified: false` because the durable user record does not override the initial false boolean.
CLI regression coverage only exercises already-shared local configs, so it misses the default-local repo plus broker-registration case that exposed the parity bug.

appliedUpdates.description: Updated `.factory/library/user-testing.md` to record that bridge-cookie bootstrap is not enough for browser-owned auth validation; auth/account slices must also exercise a real `/auth?redirect=...` browser flow to prove post-login deep-link return behavior.

Updated `.factory/library/architecture.md` to document that broker-backed project registration visibility and access resolution now depend on org/team membership scope in the shared auth-broker store.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: For auth/account handoff features, require an end-to-end browser-originated `/auth?redirect=...` validation in addition to any bridge-cookie bootstrap, so deep-link return paths are proven instead of inferred.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: The `account-shell-context-parity` review found that opening `/auth/account?bridge=1&redirect=...` successfully minted the shared shell cookie, but the actual browser-owned sign-in path from `/auth?redirect=...` still dead-ended on the handoff page because no device-flow state existed.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: When a feature contract requires browser and CLI parity, require handoff evidence of the specific browser mutation plus repo-bound CLI comparison rather than generic navigation screenshots.
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: The `project-registration-ownership-and-access-admin` feature contract required using agent-browser to register/administer a project and compare the result with repo-bound CLI ownership output, but the handoff only captured opening the unauthenticated shell and clicking the Projects nav link, which allowed the CLI parity bug to ship.
